title: Marketplace: cloud region data residency, retention & deletion Q&A
text:
Marketplace: cloud region data residency, retention & deletion Q&A

['From: Anjali Shah <anjali.shah@cloudbridge.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>; marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Tim Nguyen <tim.nguyen@marketplacevendor.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace: clarifying residency/retention/deletion questions

Hi Sergio (and Marissa),

Thanks for the walkthrough on the Marketplace listing earlier. Before we finalize the listing and the launch checklist on our side, procurement has two specific asks we need clarified for the legal/ops review:

1) Residency: For the hosted Marketplace offering, can you confirm whether customer-derived content (prompt+response pairs and embeddings) can be pinned to a single cloud region (e.g., us-west-2) for a given account, or is that routing best-effort by traffic? We need a contractual guarantee for certain customers.

2) Retention: What are the default and maximum retention windows for logs, prompt history, and embeddings? We have customers asking for 30/90/365 day options and another who requires a 5-year retention for audit copies.

3) Deletion / Worm: How does deletion propagate to backups and caches? Specifically: If a customer invokes account deletion or a record-level deletion request, what’s the SLA for irreversible deletion from primary storage, backups, and any long-term archives? Also, can you support a legal hold override?

4) Multi-cloud parity: We need parity notes for AWS/GCP/Azure—are there any features available in one but not the others (e.g., platform-managed KMS in a region, or cross-region log replication that affects deletion guarantees)?

We’ll consolidate answers into our Marketplace listing compliance page. If you can reply with a short matrix or attach existing docs, that’d be great.

Thanks,
Anjali
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
CloudBridge Partners

', 'From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Anjali Shah <anjali.shah@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com; neha_kapoor@redwood.com; Tim Nguyen <tim.nguyen@marketplacevendor.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace: clarifying residency/retention/deletion questions

Anjali — thanks for the clear list. I put together a concise matrix below and attached a detailed PDF + region mapping spreadsheet for AWS/GCP/Azure (see attachments). Short answers first, then details:

- Residency: Yes — for the hosted (Redwood API / Marketplace-hosted) offering we support region pinning at account level to a single region for new customers. We offer region guarantees for enterprise/marketplace partners via a contract appendix (adds to SLA). For existing accounts currently pinned to multiple regions we can migrate under a migration plan.

- Retention: Default logs/short-term prompt cache = 30 days. Persistent prompt/history (customer-configurable) = 30/90/365 days (configurable per-account). Long-term archival (S3/Cloud Storage) available for up to 5 years under explicit contract (adds cost).

- Deletion: Deletion from primary stores: up to 48 hours after request; propagation to cache and KV stores: within 72 hours. Backups and long-term archives: deletion from backups initiated on next scheduled retention cycle, with a certified purge process that completes within 30–45 days and is auditable. For customers requiring immediate certified purge of backups, we offer an expedited deletion (legal/ops process + additional fee) that targets a 7–14 day certified purge. We support legal hold flags — those will suspend automated deletion until released by an authorized account admin + legal request.

- Multi-cloud parity: Feature parity is high. Differences:
  * AWS: most mature KMS integrations (CloudHSM, external key policies) and native S3 Object Lock for immutability.
  * GCP: regional CMEK support in some regions lags AWS by a quarter; nearline archival behaves similarly but lifecycle APIs differ (we document).
  * Azure: managed disk snapshots and soft-delete semantics require a slightly different deletion flow; we rely on explicit snapshot purge calls for certified deletion.

Attachments: redwood-data-residency-retention-matrix.pdf (matrix + SLOs), cloud-region-mapping-aws-gcp-azure.xlsx (region/KMS parity notes).

I’ll flag a couple of open items for legal/security confirmation (see below) — looping in Neha and Marissa.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Channel/Partners
Redwood Inference

If you want a quick call I can jump on one today.

All — quick legal/product notes after a brief review of Sergio’s draft:

1) Region lock clause: Legal is comfortable with a clause that guarantees region pinning for primary storage and processing, with an explicit failure/failover carve-out. We should add language that any cross-region replication for DR will be documented and require customer opt-in for noncompliant regions. I’m attaching suggested contract wording in the Drive link (see related_links).

2) Expedited deletion: Security — Neha, we should include a simple attestation that expedited deletion will be performed under an authenticated, auditable runbook and that customers will receive a deletion certificate when complete. That certificate should include timestamped logs (audit IDs) and the list of objects purged.

3) Backups: For Marketplace listing we should avoid promising sub-30-day backup purges as default. Keep 30–45 day window in public docs and offer expedited purge as an add-on.

I’ll review the attached PDF and spreadsheet in detail and note any wording edits. If you want me to send the finalized answers to Anjali I can — Sergio, happy for you to do it if you prefer.

—Marissa
VP, Legal & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

If that all looks good we’ll proceed with the DocuSign addendum (link above) and aim to publish the listing next week. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
